items.title: Is This LLY Stock Dip Big Enough To Be Worth Buying?
items.summary: Eli Lilly (LLY) trades near $1,120, about 13% below the high it set in August, and the question is whether to step in. The stock's record after sharp falls is clean but short. That record asks for the better part of a year and more pain before it pays. And this fall is not the kind of fall that record is built on.

items.title: Why Is Pfizer Stock Paying You So Much To Wait?
items.summary: Pfizer (PFE) throws off free cash worth 7.0% of its market value a year, against 4.4% for the median S&P 500 company. Everything turns on whether the cash holds. Management's answer is a wait: it says it is well positioned to return to growth from 2029 onward. A 6.2% dividend yield over the past twelve months is what that wait pays.

items.title: AZN's Etcamah Fails Late-Stage Study for First-line Breast Cancer
items.summary: AstraZeneca's Etcamah fails to improve PFS significantly in a phase III first-line breast cancer study, while its approved use remains unaffected.

items.title: 4 High-Yield Dividend Stocks Worth Having in Your Roth IRA
items.summary: Not every high-yield dividend stock belongs in a Roth IRA, but these four generate the kind of ordinary income that makes tax-free compounding matter most. One has raised its payout 60 times in 56 years, another locks tenants into leases stretching nearly four decades into the future.

items.title: Can Pfizer Overcome Its COVID and Patent Cliff Headwinds?
items.summary: PFE faces COVID revenue declines and a patent cliff, but new products, acquisitions and a strong pipeline could fuel growth from 2029.

items.title: Pfizer’s 6% Yield Masks a Fragile Dividend Story
items.summary: Pfizer's payout looks like a safe harbor in a rough market, but the patent clock is ticking and the balance sheet leaves almost no room for error. Here is what actually has to hold true for that dividend to survive the next few years.

items.title: Big Pharma Is Pouring Billions Into China’s Biotechs
items.summary: Big Pharma firms have cut license deals worth tens of billions of dollars for cancer drugs invented in China.
